description: D15c — KEEP THE GATE, ADOPT THE REST. The prior-art sweep found that roughly half of KFT's manifest surface is already standardized, and koine restates it instead of citing it. **Adopt by reference:** MLCommons **Croissant v1.1** for dataset description (do not restate — Croissant is the ML-dataset format with real adoption across Hugging Face, Kaggle, OpenML); **ModelPack or KitOps** for weights packaging (KitOps' `model.parts[].type` already contemplates LoRA, which is exactly KFT's adaptation case); **Hugging Face `base_model`** for lineage (millions of repos already carry it and the Hub validates it — minting a koine lineage field competes with a working convention); and **Kubeflow TrainJob**'s `initializer.{dataset,model}.storageUri` as the STRUCTURAL PRECEDENT KFT §3's manifest should resemble rather than diverge from (dataset-and-model-by-reference; note TrainJob has no license, egress, trust-tier, or budget fields — which is exactly the seam KFT fills). **Genuinely empty and defensible, and therefore what KFT keeps and should say louder:** (1) the **objective x adaptation taxonomy** — OpenAI's API models only the objective axis, and Kubeflow buries adaptation in argv, so nothing else expresses the two-axis space; (2) **egress-gated placement** (§4.2, operationalizing KGP §7.2's training-set clause); (3) **graded refusal routing** — a job outside a provider's envelope is refused with a graded code that NAMES the provider that should take it; and (4) **cross-provider job portability** — nothing converts a job between Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, torchtune, TRL, and OpenAI despite 190k+ combined stars, which makes portability arguably KFT's most valuable single deliverable and it is currently unnamed in the spec. Note torchtune is officially wound down (its README carries the notice; last release v0.6.1, 2025-04-07): it belongs in a portability TARGET matrix as a legacy source format, never as a live recommended backend. Fills the Croissant / KitOps / HF base_model / Kubeflow rows of docs/upstream-standards.md. Lifecycle: KFT is candidate (0.4.0) with an owner re-ratification already pending; replacing restated fields with references is a normative change — version bump + dated changelog, Status stays candidate, and the §4 GATE's behaviour MUST NOT change (that is the uncontested part; if an edit would alter admission, stop and split it out). Coordinate with chief/71-kft-dep-repin, which owns the cross-PLANE version pins — this tasklist owns the cross-STANDARD ones. Agnostic: bind roles; external standards are named as standards, never as operational dependencies on a product. ROADMAP.md Phase F7.

userStories.title: Adopt datasets, weights, and lineage by reference
userStories.description: Stop restating what is already standardized. Each of the three surfaces below has a maintained external standard with real adoption; KFT should cite it and hold only the fields the standard has no place for.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/fine-tuning.md §3/§4 references MLCommons Croissant v1.1 for dataset description instead of restating dataset fields: a KFT job points at a Croissant-described dataset, and KFT retains ONLY the fields Croissant has no place for — at minimum the §4 license class, egress class, trust tier, and recordCount that the gate needs before fetching.

§5 references ModelPack or KitOps for weights packaging (naming KitOps' `model.parts[].type` as already covering the LoRA/adapter case) rather than specifying a bespoke weights layout, and states which KMI lineage obligations remain KFT's.
§5's model lineage references the Hugging Face `base_model` convention rather than minting a parallel koine field, with a stated rule for what happens when a base model has no Hub coordinate.

For each adoption the spec states the SEAM explicitly — what the external standard covers, what KFT adds on top, and what a producer must supply that the standard cannot express — so an implementer can tell which document to read for which field.

userStories.title: Align §3's job shape to the Kubeflow TrainJob precedent, without weakening the §4 gate
userStories.description: Kubeflow TrainJob already ships dataset-and-model-by-reference as `initializer.{dataset,model}.storageUri`. Resembling an established structure costs nothing and buys implementers a shape they already know; the gate is where KFT differs, and it must not move.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/fine-tuning.md §3's manifest shape is aligned to the TrainJob pattern of dataset-and-model-by-reference (a reference plus its describing standard, rather than inlined description), and the spec cites TrainJob as the structural precedent it follows.
The spec states what TrainJob does NOT have and KFT does — no license, egress, trust-tier, or budget fields anywhere in TrainJob — so the alignment reads as adopting a shape, not adopting a scope.

The §4 admission gate's BEHAVIOUR is unchanged: the same jobs are admitted and refused for the same reasons, and the FT-A…FT-Q findings folded by earlier passes all still hold. If any alignment edit would change an admission outcome, it is split out of this tasklist rather than landed.
schemas/finetune-job.schema.json is updated in lockstep with §3 (references replacing restated fields), its golden fixture still validates, and every schema still parses.

userStories.title: Name the four defensible claims — and make cross-provider portability a deliverable
userStories.description: KFT's genuinely unoccupied ground is currently either implicit or unstated. Say it plainly, and turn the most valuable of the four into an actual specified artefact rather than a claim.
acceptanceCriteria: specs/fine-tuning.md states its four defensible claims explicitly, each with the reason nothing else holds it: the objective x adaptation taxonomy (OpenAI models only the objective axis; Kubeflow buries adaptation in argv), egress-gated placement (§4.2 over KGP §7.2), graded refusal routing (a refusal names the provider that should take the job), and cross-provider job portability.

Portability becomes a specified artefact, not an aspiration: the spec defines a normative mapping between a KFT job manifest and the job formats of the major trainers — Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, TRL, and the OpenAI fine-tuning API — stating for each which KFT fields map, which do not, and what a lossy conversion must refuse rather than silently drop.
torchtune appears in the portability matrix ONLY as a legacy source format with its wind-down recorded (README notice; last release v0.6.1, 2025-04-07) — never as a live or recommended backend.

docs/upstream-standards.md's Croissant, KitOps/ModelPack, HF base_model, and Kubeflow TrainJob rows are filled with the versions this work was written against; fine-tuning.md bumps its version with a dated changelog entry covering all three stories, Status stays candidate, and the pending owner re-ratification and its gating scenario are restated rather than replaced.
